companyRankingLists.itemDescription: UnitedHealth Group is a diversified health care company. Its four main segments are UnitedHealthcare, which offers health care coverage to employers, small businesses, and individuals; Optum Health, which provides health care delivery and management; Optum Insight, which sells health care software and provides data analysis and consulting services; and Optum Rx, which offers pharmacy benefits management and other pharmacy services. Founded in 1974, UnitedHealth has grown rapidly, organically, and through acquisitions; it was the largest U.S. health care company by revenue in 2024.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The health insurance and health care services provider brought in $324.2 billion in revenue in 2022, making it the largest company in the U.S. health care sector.

  • As of the end of Q1 2023, UnitedHealthcare, the company’s insurance arm, served nearly 2 million more people than a year earlier, for a total of 52.9 million.

  • Revenue per consumer served in UnitedHealth’s Optum health services division increased 34% in Q1 2023 over the same quarter a year earlier.

  • In March 2023, the U.S. Justice Department dropped an appeal that challenged UnitedHealth Group’s $8 billion acquisition of data analytics company Change Healthcare.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: UnitedHealth Group maintains its status as the largest health insurance provider in the U.S., and 2021 was a year of significant growth. The company served 2.2 million more people than in the previous year and saw a 12% rise in revenue year over year, to $287 billion. Pharmacy benefits management company Optum, one of UnitedHealth’s subsidiaries, delivered a 33% increase in revenue per consumer. Adding a 16th company to its vast portfolio of acquisitions, UnitedHealth bought Golden Valley–based health insurer PreferredOne to compete for business in its home state of Minnesota.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The Minnesota-based health insurer thrived during the pandemic year, climbing two spots on the list. While widespread layoffs led to a decline in the number of individuals covered by its commercial insurance, the firm’s 6.2% revenue growth was powered by greater enrollment in its Medicare Advantage and Medicaid plans, and by the strong performance of Optum, its sprawling $136 billion health services business. Despite the costs of covering COVID patients, UnitedHealth’s profits jumped 11.3%, owing to members’ decreased use of health services during the pandemic. In an abrupt leadership change, Andrew Witty, who previously ran the company’s Optum division, became CEO in February 2021.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The largest health insurer in the U.S. fired on all cylinders in 2019, with a 7% increase in annual revenues that brought the company's haul to $242 billion. Its UnitedHealthcare division grew by $10 billion last year, but the insurer's real and not-so-secret weapon continues to be its Optum unit, which provides an array of health care services including data analytics and pharmacy benefits management. Optum revenues climbed 12% year-over-year, to $113 billion. UnitedHealth Group also has considerable ambitions for its Medicare Advantage business, which had its best-ever enrollment last year, adding 325,000 elderly Americans.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
